captions_note: the timeline's labels are the effect itself, not speech, so the reel's captions stay on in the buyer's style. The timeline sits in the chest band: add the slot with the fx_add.py --caption-y value build.py prints (the captions move to the line above the timeline). If build.py says there is no room for a caption line, add the slot with --captions hide instead
in_a_reel: before the first build set FONT, WEIGHT, CASE, TEXT, ACCENT and PALETTE in the STYLE block at the top of build.py to the buyer's caption or overall style (ACCENT = the reel's accent colour)

BURN_AT is a word the speaker says in the slot. The slot needs 30 frames or more before it (72 for the cursor edits) and 30 after it. Frame 0 and the last frame are plain footage by construction; the effect cannot end on a cut
DIM darkens the whole picture while the timeline is up and is back before the slot ends. Set DIM = 0 when the reel's overall style is already dark or the buyer does not want the room dimmed
labels and clip names are generic track names or the speaker's own words: no app name, no logo, no invented names or numbers
steps: run build.py words      # 1. every word with its frame -> BURN_AT in the CLIP block; reel style -> the STYLE block
run build.py SAFE=1      # 2. measures the face, places the timeline, page with the guide. Read the !! lines, LOOK at work/layout.jpg
hf lint      # must be 0 errors (a "file too large" warning is normal)
run check.py      # 4. frame count, plain edges, burn frame, face, safe zone, sheet, stills, phone copy
